items.stem: Which of the following does a green plant need to make food by photosynthesis?

explain.why: Oxygen and sugar are made by the plant. They are not what it needs to start.
Oxygen is not a raw material, and light is needed too.
Sugar is made by photosynthesis, so it is not a requirement.

solution: Photosynthesis needs light energy, water and carbon dioxide.

items.stem: Which gas does a plant take in from the air for photosynthesis?

explain.why: Oxygen is given out by photosynthesis.
Plants do not use nitrogen gas to make food.
Plants take in liquid water through the roots, not water vapour for food.

solution: The plant takes in carbon dioxide from the air.

items.stem: Which gas is given out by a plant during photosynthesis?

explain.why: This is taken in by the plant.
Photosynthesis does not give out nitrogen.
Photosynthesis does not give out hydrogen.

solution: Oxygen is a product of photosynthesis.

items.stem: Which of the following is the food made by a plant in photosynthesis?

explain.why: Oxygen is a gas given out. It is not food.
Carbon dioxide is taken in as a raw material.
Water is taken in as a raw material.

solution: Photosynthesis makes sugar, which the plant uses as food.

items.stem: Which part of a plant mainly makes food by photosynthesis?

explain.why: Roots take in water. They are underground and get no light.
The stem carries water and sugar. It does not mainly make food.
Seeds can grow into new plants. They do not mainly make food.

solution: Leaves are flat and take in a lot of light, so most food is made there.

items.stem: Which form of energy do plants need to make food?

explain.why: Plants do not use sound to make food.
Plants do not need movement energy to make food.
Plants do not use electricity to make food.

solution: Plants use light energy, usually from the Sun.

items.stem: From where does a plant take in the water it uses for photosynthesis?

explain.why: Most of the water comes from the soil.
The Sun gives light, not water.
Flowers do not take in water for food.

solution: Roots take in water, which travels up the stem to the leaves.

items.stem: A potted plant is kept in a dark cupboard for many days. What will happen to the plant?
options: It makes more food than before
It cannot make food and becomes weak
It makes more oxygen than before

explain.why: Without light a plant cannot make food.
Oxygen is given out only when photosynthesis takes place.
Without food the plant becomes weak.

solution: Without light, photosynthesis cannot take place.

items.stem: Why do plants need light?
options: To get energy to make food
To take in water from the soil

explain.why: Light is not breathed in.
Roots take in water without light.
Plants take in carbon dioxide. They do not make it for food.

solution: Light provides the energy for photosynthesis.

items.stem: Which equation correctly shows photosynthesis?
options: Sugar + oxygen, in light, makes carbon dioxide + water
Oxygen + water, in light, makes sugar + carbon dioxide
Sugar + water, in light, makes oxygen + carbon dioxide
Carbon dioxide + water, in light, makes sugar + oxygen

explain.why: This is the wrong way round. Plants make sugar from carbon dioxide and water.
Oxygen is given out, and carbon dioxide is taken in.
Sugar is a product, not a raw material.

solution: Raw materials: carbon dioxide and water. Products: sugar and oxygen.

items.stem: Which one of the following is NOT needed by a plant for photosynthesis?

explain.why: Light energy is needed.
Water is a raw material.
Carbon dioxide is a raw material.

solution: Oxygen is a product of photosynthesis, so it is not needed.

items.stem: A leaf is partly covered with foil and placed in bright light. Part P is covered with foil and part Q is not. Which part cannot make food?

explain.why: Part Q gets light, so it can make food.
Part Q is not covered, so it gets light.
Part P is covered, so it gets no light.

solution: Foil stops light from reaching part P, so it cannot photosynthesise.

items.stem: A farmer wants her vegetable plants to make more food. Which of the following will help?
options: Planting them in a dark room
Planting them where they get plenty of sunlight and water
Covering them with a plastic sheet that blocks the light

explain.why: Without light plants cannot make food.
Plants need water to make food.
Blocking light stops photosynthesis.

solution: Light and water are needed for photosynthesis.

items.stem: When does photosynthesis mainly take place?
options: At night, when the plant is in the dark
In the day, when there is light
Only when it is raining hard
Only in the late evening hours

explain.why: No light means no photosynthesis.
Rain is not needed, only water in the soil.
Light is needed, and it is stronger in the day.

solution: Light is needed, so photosynthesis happens in the day.

items.stem: A plant makes more sugar than it needs. What happens to the extra sugar?
options: Some is stored as starch in roots, stems and fruits
It is given out through the leaves into the air as a gas
It is turned into water and given out from the roots
It is thrown away through the roots into the soil

explain.why: Sugar is not given out. Oxygen is the gas given out.
Sugar is not turned into water.
The plant does not waste its food.

solution: The plant stores extra food as starch.

items.stem: Which of the following can make its own food?

explain.why: Animals cannot make their own food.
A mushroom takes food from dead things.
Animals cannot make their own food.

solution: Only green plants make food using light.

items.stem: Which solution is used to test a leaf for starch?

explain.why: Salt does not show starch.
Vinegar does not show starch.
Soap does not show starch.

solution: Iodine solution turns blue-black when starch is present.

items.stem: A leaf that has been making food in the light is tested with iodine solution. What colour does the leaf turn if it has starch?

explain.why: Yellow-brown is the colour of iodine when there is no starch.
Iodine does not turn red with starch.
Iodine does not turn leaves green.

solution: Starch makes iodine turn blue-black.

items.stem: A pondweed in bright light gives out tiny bubbles. Which gas is in the bubbles?

explain.why: The pondweed takes this in.
Photosynthesis does not give out nitrogen.
The bubbles are mainly oxygen, a product of photosynthesis.

solution: The bubbles are oxygen given out in photosynthesis.

items.stem: Which gas must be dissolved in the water for a water plant to make food?

explain.why: Plants do not use nitrogen to make food.
Plants do not use hydrogen to make food.
Oxygen is given out by the plant. It is not a raw material.

solution: Water plants take in dissolved carbon dioxide.

items.stem: Which gas that animals need to breathe is added to the air by plants in the day?

explain.why: Plants take this in during the day.
Plants do not add nitrogen.
Plants do not give out hydrogen.

solution: Plants give out oxygen when they make food in the light.

items.stem: A plant on a window sill gets plenty of light but no water for a week. What will most likely happen?
options: It makes more food than before
It cannot make enough food and it wilts
It gives out more oxygen than before
It takes in more water through its leaves

explain.why: Water is a raw material, so less water means less food.
Less food made means less oxygen given out.
Without water in the soil it cannot take in more.

solution: Without water, photosynthesis slows down or stops.

items.stem: Why are the leaves of a plant usually flat and wide?
options: To take in more water from the air

explain.why: Most water is taken in by the roots.
Leaf shape does not add weight.
Leaves take carbon dioxide in.

solution: A big flat surface takes in more light for photosynthesis.

items.stem: A plant is kept in the dark for a day. Then one leaf is partly covered with foil as shown and the plant is put in bright light for several hours. The leaf is then tested for starch. Which part turns blue-black?

explain.why: P is white and has no green, so it cannot make food.
R is green but it is covered with foil, so it gets no light.
P has no green and R gets no light, so neither makes starch.

solution: Only Q is green and gets light, so it makes starch.

explain.why: Q is green and gets light, so it can make starch.
R also cannot make starch because it gets no light.
Q can make starch.

solution: P has no green part, and R is covered, so it gets no light.

options: To make the leaves make more starch
To make the leaves take in more water
To use up the starch already in the leaves
To kill the plant so it can be tested

solution: The plant uses up its starch in the dark, so any starch found later was made during the test.

To remove the green colour so the colour change shows
To add water to the leaf so it is soft
To turn the iodine solution blue-black at once

explain.why: Boiling kills the leaf. It cannot make starch.
Alcohol does not add water.
Iodine turns blue-black only if starch is present.

solution: The green colour would hide the blue-black colour.

Starch, because it has light and water
Starch, because the dish gives it extra carbon dioxide
No starch, because the dish takes in the oxygen

explain.why: Carbon dioxide is also needed. Without it no food is made.
The dish takes carbon dioxide in. It does not give any.
Oxygen is not needed to make starch. The missing carbon dioxide is the problem.

solution: Without carbon dioxide, photosynthesis cannot take place, so the leaves have no starch.

items.stem: A plant is sealed in a clear glass jar and placed in bright light. It stays alive for many weeks. Which statement best explains this?
options: It takes in food from the glass of the jar
It uses the oxygen it gives out to make food
It needs no light, water or air to live
It uses light to make food and oxygen from water and carbon dioxide

explain.why: Glass does not give food.
Oxygen is not a raw material for food.
A plant needs light, water and carbon dioxide.

solution: The plant makes food in the light and the water and gases in the jar are reused.

items.stem: The leaves of a plant that was kept in a dark cupboard for two weeks turn pale. Why?
options: It made too much food in the dark
It took in too much carbon dioxide
It could not make food in the dark

explain.why: Without light it makes no food.
It did not take in too much of anything.
Oxygen was not what it was missing. Light was.

solution: Without light there is no photosynthesis.

items.stem: Small plants grow poorly on the floor of a thick forest. What is the most likely reason?
options: They get far too much light from above
They get very little light for photosynthesis
They are surrounded by far too much carbon dioxide
They have no roots to take in water

explain.why: The forest floor is shady.
Carbon dioxide in the air is about the same everywhere.
They have roots, but they lack light.

solution: The trees above block most of the light.

items.stem: Two leaves on a plant were tested for starch after a day on a sunny windowsill. The results are shown. What can be concluded?
options: Light is needed for the leaf to make starch
Water is needed for the leaf to make starch
Foil makes a leaf make starch
Carbon dioxide is not needed for the leaf to make starch

explain.why: Water was not tested in this experiment.
The covered leaf made no starch.
Carbon dioxide was not tested.

solution: The covered leaf Y got no light and had no starch.

options: Light is needed for the plant to make starch
Carbon dioxide is needed to make starch
Water is needed for the plant to make starch

explain.why: Both plants had the same light.
Plant Q did not make starch without water.
Carbon dioxide was not changed in the test.

solution: Only the water was different, and Q made no starch.

items.stem: In the day, which gas is higher in the air around a healthy plant in bright light than at night?

explain.why: In the day the plant takes this in, so there is less of it.
The plant does not change the amount of nitrogen.
Plants do not give out hydrogen.

solution: The plant gives out oxygen in photosynthesis.

items.stem: An aquarium has fish and a water plant. How does the plant help the fish in bright light?
options: It takes in oxygen from the fish and gives out carbon dioxide
It takes in carbon dioxide from the fish and gives out oxygen
It gives out sugar into the water for the fish to breathe
It stops the fish from giving out carbon dioxide

explain.why: In the light the plant takes in carbon dioxide and gives out oxygen.
Fish breathe oxygen. Sugar is not breathed.
The plant does not stop this.

solution: The fish give out carbon dioxide, which the plant uses. The plant gives out oxygen, which the fish breathe.

items.stem: Which statement about gases and plants in the day is correct?
options: A plant in bright light takes in more carbon dioxide than it gives out
A plant in bright light gives out more carbon dioxide than it takes in
A plant in bright light takes in oxygen only
A plant in bright light takes in and gives out no gases

explain.why: Photosynthesis uses up carbon dioxide.
It also gives out oxygen.
It exchanges gases with the air.

solution: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide faster than the plant gives it out.

items.stem: A potato plant makes sugar in its leaves and stores starch in the underground potatoes. How does the sugar reach the potatoes?
options: It is carried down through the air
It leaks out of the leaves into the soil
The potatoes make their own sugar from the soil
It is carried down through tubes in the stem

explain.why: Sugar does not travel through the air.
Sugar does not leak out of the leaves.
Underground parts get no light, so they cannot photosynthesise.

solution: Tubes in the stem carry food from the leaves to other parts.

items.stem: Which statement describes the change in energy during photosynthesis?
options: Energy stored in sugar is changed into light energy
Heat energy is changed into sound energy
Light energy is changed into energy stored in sugar
Kinetic energy is changed into light energy

explain.why: This is the wrong way round. The plant takes in light.
Plants do not make sound from heat in photosynthesis.
Photosynthesis does not use kinetic energy.

solution: The plant takes in light energy and stores it in the sugar it makes.

items.stem: A plant kept in the dark for two days is tested with iodine solution. What does the leaf show?
options: The leaf turns blue-black because it has starch
The leaf stays brown because there is no starch
The leaf turns red because it has sugar
The leaf turns green because it has water

explain.why: No light means no starch is made, and the old starch is used up.
Iodine does not turn red.
Iodine does not turn leaves green.

solution: In the dark the plant uses up its starch and makes no new starch.

items.stem: Which of the following does the sugar made by a plant help the plant to do?
options: Take in light from the Sun

explain.why: Leaves take in light without using sugar.
Plants do not make carbon dioxide this way.
Sugar does not help plants to absorb water from the air.

solution: Plants use sugar for energy and growth, and store the extra.

items.stem: Four tubes contain the same indicator solution. A tube wrapped in foil is kept in the dark. Which two tubes should be compared to find out whether pondweed needs light to take in carbon dioxide?

explain.why: A and C differ in the pondweed, not in the light.
B and D differ in the pondweed, and both are in the dark.
C and D have no pondweed, so they cannot test the pondweed.

solution: A and B both have pondweed and only the light is different.

options: The pondweed made more oxygen in the dark than in the light

The foil around the tube gave out carbon dioxide into the water

Whether there is a dish that takes in carbon dioxide
The amount of starch in the leaves

This is the change he makes on purpose.
This is what he finds out at the end.

solution: Only the carbon dioxide should change.

options: Oxygen increases and carbon dioxide decreases
Both oxygen and carbon dioxide increase
Oxygen decreases and carbon dioxide increases

explain.why: In the dark there is no photosynthesis to make oxygen or use carbon dioxide.
The plant uses oxygen in the dark, so it does not increase.
The plant is alive and takes in oxygen and gives out carbon dioxide.

solution: With no photosynthesis, the plant still uses oxygen and gives out carbon dioxide.

The fish in Q will have more oxygen because the pondweed is resting

The lamp is on and the pondweed is in the light.

solution: A nearer lamp gives brighter light, so more oxygen bubbles are given out.

options: It makes food in the light and uses some of its food for energy
It makes food only and never uses any of its food
It uses food for energy only during the night
It makes food at night and stores it in the day

explain.why: Plants use food for energy all the time.
Plants use food for energy day and night.
Food is made only when there is light.

solution: Plants make food in the light, and use food for energy all the time.

items.stem: A sweet potato plant stores starch in its roots. Where did the plant first make the sugar that became this starch?
options: In the stem under the soil

explain.why: Roots are underground in the dark, so they cannot photosynthesise.
Soil does not make sugar.
A stem under the soil gets no light.

solution: Sugar is made in the leaves in the light and carried down to the roots for storage.

items.stem: Water plants in a pond grow best in the water near the surface. Why?
options: They get more soil to grow in near the surface
They get much less carbon dioxide near the surface
They get more light for photosynthesis near the surface
They have no need for light, so depth does not matter

explain.why: Soil is at the bottom of the pond.
Less carbon dioxide would not help them.
Plants always need light to make food.

solution: Light cannot reach deep into the water.

items.stem:
Which of the following would help a plant in a greenhouse to make more food?
A: More light
B: More water
C: More carbon dioxide
D: More oxygen

explain.why: Oxygen is a product of photosynthesis, so more of it does not help.
More light also helps, and more oxygen does not.
Water and carbon dioxide help too, and oxygen does not.

solution: Light, water and carbon dioxide are what a plant needs.

items.stem: A plant has leaves with white patches. Why does it make less food than a plant with all-green leaves?
options: The white parts cannot make food, so less of each leaf can
The white parts take in much less water than green parts
The white parts make more oxygen than green parts do
The white parts block light from the green parts

explain.why: The roots take in the water.
Parts that cannot make food make no oxygen.
The white parts do not shade the green parts.

solution: Only the green parts make food.

items.stem: The graph shows the sugar made by a plant in different numbers of hours of light. How much sugar will be made in 5 hours, if the plant keeps making sugar in the same way?

explain.why: 20 units is the amount for 4 hours.
30 units is the amount for 6 hours.
The plant makes 5 units in each hour, so 5 hours gives 25 units.

solution: The plant makes 5 units each hour, so in 5 hours it makes 25 units.

items.stem: Which is the best way to make the results of a pondweed bubble-counting experiment more reliable?
options: Count the bubbles for only 5 seconds
Repeat each test several times and take the average
Use a different pondweed each time
Change the lamp distance and the temperature together

explain.why: A short count gives less reliable results.
A different plant adds another difference between tests.
Changing two things at once makes the result unclear.

solution: Repeating gives an average that is less affected by one odd result.

items.stem: Which row correctly gives one raw material and one product of photosynthesis?
options: Raw material: sugar; product: carbon dioxide
Raw material: carbon dioxide; product: water

explain.why: Oxygen is a product, not a raw material.
Sugar is a product, and carbon dioxide is a raw material.
Water is a raw material, not a product.

solution: Water and carbon dioxide are raw materials. Sugar and oxygen are products.

items.stem: A plant under a jar is covered with a black cloth for several days, as shown. It makes no starch in its leaves. Why?
options: It has been given far too much water
It has far too much carbon dioxide
It gives out too much oxygen under the jar
The cloth stops light from reaching the plant

explain.why: Nothing in the picture says it has too much water.
It is not short of anything but light.
It gives out no oxygen without light.

solution: Without light there is no photosynthesis, so no starch is made.
